title: Swe mid scenario memory leak
question: Memory usage on one of your backend services climbs steadily over hours and the process eventually gets OOM-killed and restarted. How do you find the leak?
idealAnswer:
Recognizes the gradual, monotonic growth pattern as a classic memory leak signature (something is being retained and never released), not a load spike or normal GC sawtooth pattern

Proposes using a memory profiler or heap snapshot tool appropriate to the language/runtime to see what object types are accumulating over time

Suggests comparing heap snapshots taken at two points in time to see what's growing, rather than just staring at total memory usage

Names plausible concrete causes: an ever-growing cache or in-memory collection with no eviction, event listeners/subscriptions that are added but never removed, or unclosed resources like connections accumulating

Mentions the restart as only masking the symptom, treating the automatic OOM-restart as a stopgap while root-causing, not as an acceptable long-term fix
